title: Mild paneer bhurji wrap
summary: Crumbled paneer cooked with soft onion, ginger and passata in gentle spices, rolled up warm in a soft white flatbread with yoghurt.
ingredients: 2 large soft white flour tortillas or flatbreads
steps: Warm the oil in a frying pan and cook the onion gently for 10 minutes until very soft. Add the garlic, ginger, turmeric and curry powder for 1 minute.
Stir in the passata and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the paneer and milk and cook for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until hot and soft. Stir in the lemon juice and coriander, if using, and season with salt.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 20 seconds each side.
Spoon the paneer down the middle of each, add a spoonful of yoghurt and roll up.
tip: Grating the paneer and adding a splash of milk keeps it soft and creamy rather than squeaky. Choose plain white flatbreads with a short ingredient list.
swaps: Use 4 eggs, scrambled softly in the spiced onion, instead of paneer
Use crumbled firm tofu instead of paneer

storage.text: The bhurji filling keeps in the fridge for 2 days; reheat until piping hot and wrap in a freshly warmed tortilla. Don't freeze.

title: Tofu katsu curry
summary: Oven-crisp panko tofu with a smooth, sweet Japanese-style curry sauce and fluffy white rice.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) and line a tray with baking paper.
Cut the tofu into 8 slabs. Dip each in the 3 tbsp flour, then the egg, then press into the panko.
Lay on the tray, drizzle with 2 tbsp of the oil and bake for 25 minutes, turning halfway, until golden.
Meanwhile, soften the onion and carrots in the remaining oil for 10 minutes. Add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Stir in the curry powder and the 1 tbsp flour, then gradually add the stock, grated apple, soy and honey. Simmer for 15 minutes until the carrots are very soft.
Blend the sauce until completely smooth, adding a splash of water if it is too thick.
Cook the rice according to the packet instructions.
Slice the tofu, lay it on the rice and spoon some of the sauce over so the crumb softens a little; serve the rest alongside.
tip: The sauce is blended until silky, so there are no pieces of onion or carrot to chew. Spooning sauce over the baked crumb softens it, and chew each mouthful well.
swaps: Use thick slices of halloumi instead of tofu (skip the egg wash and just dust in flour and panko)
Serve the sauce over soft udon noodles instead of rice

storage.text: Make a double batch of the curry sauce: it keeps for 3 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer. The baked tofu keeps for 2 days in the fridge; re-crisp in a hot oven. Cool leftover rice within 1 hour, keep in the fridge, eat within 1 day and reheat only once until piping hot. Don't freeze cooked rice.

title: Malaysian-style tofu & potato curry
summary: A fragrant, mild coconut curry with lemongrass, turmeric and warm spices, inspired by Malaysian kari.
ingredients: 1 lemongrass stalk, bashed with a rolling pin
600g potatoes, peeled and cut into 3cm chunks
steps: Blitz the onion, garlic and ginger to a paste in a mini chopper or blender with a splash of water.
Heat the oil in a large pan and cook the paste with the lemongrass, cinnamon and star anise for 8 minutes until soft, sweet and lightly golden.
Stir in the curry powder and turmeric for 1 minute.
Add the potatoes, carrots, coconut milk and stock. Simmer, partly covered, for 20 minutes until the vegetables are very tender.
Add the tofu, soy and sugar and simmer for 5 minutes more.
Remove the lemongrass, cinnamon and star anise, stir in the lime juice and serve with rice.
tip: The whole spices and lemongrass give lots of flavour but are lifted out before serving, so nothing woody is left behind. Choose a coconut milk with a short ingredient list, or use light coconut milk if you prefer it less rich.
swaps: Use peeled butternut squash instead of carrots
Swap the tofu for 4 halved hard-boiled eggs, added at the end

storage.text: Great for batch cooking. Keep the curry in the fridge for 3 days or freeze in portions for 3 months (the potatoes may soften a little). Defrost overnight in the fridge and reheat until piping hot. Cook rice fresh; if you keep leftover rice, cool it within 1 hour, eat within 1 day, reheat once and don't freeze it.

title: Thai-style coconut noodles with tofu
summary: Silky rice noodles in a fragrant lemongrass, ginger and lime coconut broth, made without curry paste.
ingredients: 1 lemongrass stalk, bashed with a rolling pin
1 small bunch fresh coriander, stalks very finely chopped (leaves very finely chopped, optional)
steps: Soak or cook the rice noodles according to the packet, then drain.
Heat the oil in a large pan and gently fry the lemongrass, garlic, ginger and chopped coriander stalks for 2 minutes.
Stir in the turmeric and ground coriander, then pour in the coconut milk and stock. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the tofu and courgette and simmer for 8 minutes until the courgette is very soft.
Stir in the spinach until wilted, then season with the soy, sugar and lime juice. Remove the lemongrass.
Divide the noodles between bowls, ladle over the broth and scatter with a little very finely chopped coriander leaf, if you like.
tip: Shop-bought Thai curry pastes often contain chilli and shrimp paste, so this builds the flavour from lemongrass, ginger and lime instead. Cooking the coriander stalks keeps their flavour without any raw leaves.
swaps: Use soft-boiled eggs instead of tofu
Swap the courgette for peeled, thinly sliced carrot

storage.text: Best eaten fresh. Keep leftover broth and noodles separately in the fridge for up to 2 days and reheat the broth until piping hot before pouring over. Not suitable for freezing.

title: Mild aloo paneer curry
summary: Tender potatoes and soft paneer in a gently spiced, creamy tomato sauce.
ingredients: 600g potatoes, peeled and cut into 2cm cubes
Warm plain naan or white rice, to serve
steps: Heat the oil and butter in a large pan and cook the onion gently for 10 minutes until very soft.
Add the garlic, ginger, cumin, ground coriander, turmeric and garam masala and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the passata and water, add the potatoes and simmer, covered, for 20 minutes until the potatoes are very tender.
Add the paneer and simmer for 5 minutes until it is soft and warmed through.
Stir in the cream and lemon juice, season with salt and serve with naan or rice.
tip: Simmering the paneer in the sauce, rather than frying it, keeps it soft. Blend the sauce before adding the potatoes if you'd like it completely smooth.
swaps: Use cubes of firm tofu instead of paneer
Use 2 tbsp natural yoghurt instead of the cream (stir in off the heat)

storage.text: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge. To freeze, cool before adding the cream and freeze in portions for up to 3 months; defrost in the fridge, reheat until piping hot, then stir in the cream. If serving with rice, cool any leftover rice within 1 hour, eat within 1 day, reheat once and don't freeze it.

title: One-pot creamy tomato orzo
summary: Orzo simmered in tomato and stock until creamy, finished with mascarpone, spinach and melting mozzarella.
steps: Warm the oil in a wide, deep pan and cook the garlic for 1 minute without browning.
Add the orzo, passata, stock and oregano. Bring to a simmer and cook for 12–14 minutes, stirring often, until the orzo is very soft and most of the liquid is absorbed.
Stir in the spinach until wilted, then the mascarpone. Season with salt and pepper.
Dot the mozzarella over the top, cover with a lid for 2 minutes until melted, and serve.
tip: Everything cooks in one pan and the orzo turns soft and risotto-like. Add an extra splash of stock for a looser, softer finish.
swaps: Use cream cheese instead of mascarpone
Stir in 100g ricotta instead of the mozzarella

storage.text: Keeps for 2 days in the fridge. Freeze portions (ideally before adding the mozzarella) for up to 2 months. Defrost in the fridge and reheat with a splash of water until piping hot, adding fresh mozzarella if you like.

title: Moong dal khichdi
summary: A soothing, porridge-soft Indian one-pot of white rice and split yellow lentils with ghee and turmeric.
steps: Rinse the rice and moong dal together in a sieve until the water runs clear.
Melt the ghee in a large pan and stir in the cumin, turmeric and ginger for 30 seconds.
Add the rice, dal, carrot, water and salt. Bring to the boil, then cover and simmer gently for 30–35 minutes, stirring now and then, until very soft and porridge-like.
Mash lightly with the back of a spoon, loosen with a little hot water if needed and serve.
tip: Split moong dal and white rice cook down until very soft, making this a traditional comforting meal. Keep the ghee to a spoonful so it stays light.
swaps: Use red lentils instead of moong dal
Swap the carrot for peeled, diced courgette

storage.text: Contains cooked rice: cool within 1 hour, keep in the fridge and eat within 1 day. Reheat only once, with a splash of water, until piping hot. Don't freeze.

title: Steamed silken tofu with ginger soy
summary: Warm, wobbly silken tofu with a light ginger and soy dressing, served over soft rice with wilted spinach.
steps: Cook the rice according to the packet, adding an extra splash of water for a softer result.
Carefully slide the tofu onto a heatproof plate that fits in a steamer (or a plate set on a rack in a lidded pan of simmering water). Steam for 8 minutes.
Wilt the spinach in a pan with a splash of water for 1–2 minutes, then squeeze out excess water.
Mix the soy, water, honey, ginger and sesame oil in a small pan and warm through.
Spoon the rice into bowls, add the spinach, then cut the tofu into large pieces, place on top and spoon over the dressing.
tip: Silken tofu needs no chewing and the ginger dressing is light, so this is a calm, easy dinner. Toasted sesame oil is just the oil — no seeds.
swaps: Serve over soft udon noodles instead of rice
Swap the spinach for peeled, steamed courgette

storage.text: Best eaten straight away. If you keep leftover rice, cool it within 1 hour, keep in the fridge, eat within 1 day and reheat only once until piping hot. Don't freeze.

title: Gnocchi with silky courgette sauce
summary: Pillowy gnocchi coated in a pale green sauce of blended peeled courgette, ricotta and a little cheese.
ingredients: 20g vegetarian Italian-style hard cheese, finely grated
steps: Warm the oil in a pan and gently cook the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the courgettes and stock, cover and cook for 10–12 minutes until completely soft.
Blend the courgettes with the ricotta, cheese, lemon zest and a squeeze of the juice until smooth. Season with salt and pepper, adding more lemon to taste.
Cook the gnocchi in boiling salted water until they float, about 2–3 minutes, then drain.
Toss the gnocchi with the warm sauce and finish with a little very finely chopped basil if you like.
tip: Peeling and blending the courgette gives a smooth, light sauce with no skins. Choose gnocchi with a short ingredient list.
swaps: Toss the sauce through small pasta shapes instead of gnocchi
Use cream cheese instead of ricotta

storage.text: Best eaten fresh. Keep leftovers in the fridge for up to 2 days and reheat gently with a splash of water until piping hot. Not suitable for freezing.

title: Sweet carrot & thyme risotto
summary: A bright orange, creamy risotto with finely grated carrot melted right into the rice.
ingredients: 30g vegetarian Italian-style hard cheese, finely grated
steps: Heat the oil and butter in a wide pan and cook the onion gently for 8 minutes until very soft.
Add the carrots and thyme and cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until the carrot starts to collapse.
Stir in the rice for 1 minute, then add the stock a ladle at a time, stirring and letting each addition be absorbed before adding the next. This takes about 20 minutes.
When the rice is very tender and creamy, stir in the cheese, season with salt and pepper and serve.
tip: Finely grated carrot practically dissolves into the risotto, so you get the sweetness without firm pieces. Cook the rice a few minutes longer than usual for an extra-soft texture.
swaps: Use peeled, grated courgette instead of carrot
Swap the hard cheese for 2 tbsp mascarpone

storage.text: Contains cooked rice: cool within 1 hour, keep in the fridge and eat within 1 day. Reheat only once, with a splash of stock, until piping hot. Don't freeze.

title: Japanese-style simmered tofu & potatoes
summary: A homely nikujaga-style pot of potatoes, carrots and tofu gently simmered in a sweet soy broth.
ingredients: 600g potatoes, peeled and cut into 3cm chunks
2 carrots, peeled and cut into 1cm slices
steps: Heat the oil in a wide pan and cook the onion gently for 8–10 minutes until completely soft.
Add the potatoes and carrots, then pour in the stock, soy, mirin and sugar.
Bring to a simmer, cover with a lid slightly ajar and cook for 20–25 minutes until the potatoes and carrots are fork-soft.
Add the tofu and simmer for 5 minutes more, spooning the broth over.
Stir in the spinach until just wilted and serve in bowls with some of the broth.
tip: Everything is simmered rather than fried, and the potatoes and carrots become fork-soft. Keep the carrot slices thin so they soften at the same rate as the potatoes.
swaps: Use peeled chunks of butternut squash instead of carrots
Add 4 halved hard-boiled eggs instead of tofu

storage.text: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge and tastes even better the next day. Reheat until piping hot. Not ideal for freezing as the potatoes and tofu turn spongy.

title: Red lentil & aubergine moussaka
summary: Layers of soft peeled aubergine, potato and cinnamon-spiced lentil sauce under a golden cheesy topping.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Brush the aubergine slices with 2 tbsp of the oil and roast on a lined tray for 25 minutes until very soft.
Meanwhile, boil the potato slices for 6 minutes until just tender, then drain.
Soften the onion in the remaining oil for 10 minutes. Add the garlic, lentils, passata, tomato purée, stock, oregano and cinnamon and simmer for 20 minutes until thick. Season with salt and pepper.
Make the sauce: melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the milk and simmer until thick. Add the nutmeg and half the cheese.
Layer the potatoes, lentil sauce and aubergine in a large ovenproof dish, finishing with lentils. Pour over the white sauce and scatter with the remaining cheese.
Bake for 35 minutes until golden and bubbling. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.
tip: Peeling the aubergine and roasting it until soft removes the tough skin. Lentils make a soft filling with no chewy pieces.
swaps: Use peeled courgette slices instead of aubergine
Top with 2 beaten eggs mixed into the white sauce for a firmer, more traditional topping (don't freeze if you do)

storage.text: Ideal for batch cooking. Keeps for 3 days in the fridge or freeze whole or in portions for 3 months. Defrost in the fridge overnight and reheat until piping hot.

title: Cheese, onion & potato pie
summary: A classic northern-style pie of soft, cheesy potato and sweet onion in crisp shortcrust pastry.
ingredients: 700g floury potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
steps: Boil the potatoes for 15 minutes until soft, drain and mash until smooth.
Meanwhile, melt the butter and cook the onion gently for 10 minutes until very soft and sweet.
Mix the potato, onion, cheese, milk and nutmeg. Season with salt and pepper and leave to cool a little.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Roll out two-thirds of the pastry on a floured surface and line a 23cm pie dish.
Spoon in the filling, roll out the remaining pastry for a lid, seal the edges and cut a small steam hole. Brush with egg.
Bake for 35–40 minutes until deep golden. Rest for 10 minutes before slicing.
tip: The filling is soft and smooth; cook the onion until it melts so there are no firm pieces. Shortcrust needs chewing, so eat it slowly — or use the mash-topped swap on a sore day. Pick a shop-bought pastry made with butter and a short ingredient list.
swaps: Use a mash topping instead of the pastry lid
Swap half the cheddar for crumbled Lancashire cheese

storage.text: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge. Freeze whole or in slices for up to 3 months, wrapped well. Defrost in the fridge and reheat in the oven until piping hot so the pastry crisps up again.

title: Creamy leek & cheddar pot pie
summary: Soft leeks, potato and carrot in a cheesy sauce under a golden puff pastry lid.
ingredients: 2 leeks (white and pale green parts only), halved lengthways and very finely sliced
steps: Melt the butter in a large pan and cook the leeks and carrots gently, covered, for 15 minutes until very soft.
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes for 10 minutes until tender, then drain.
Stir the flour into the leeks for 1 minute, then gradually stir in the milk and stock. Add the thyme and simmer for 5 minutes until thick.
Stir in the potatoes, spinach and cheese and season with salt and pepper. Tip into a pie dish and leave to cool for 10 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Lay the pastry over the dish, trim, crimp the edges, cut a steam hole and brush with egg.
Bake for 25–30 minutes until puffed and golden.
tip: Slice the leeks finely and cook them slowly until silky so there are no stringy bits. Choose an all-butter puff pastry with a short ingredient list.
swaps: Add 200g cubed firm tofu to the filling for extra protein
Top with mash instead of pastry

storage.text: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge. The filling freezes well for 3 months: defrost in the fridge, add a fresh pastry lid and bake until piping hot. Reheat leftovers in the oven until piping hot.

title: Smoky red lentil & butter bean stew
summary: A thick, smoky-sweet tomato stew of red lentils and carrot, made creamy with blended butter beans.
steps: Soften the onion and carrots in the oil for 10 minutes. Add the garlic, paprika and cumin and stir for 1 minute.
Blend the butter beans with 200ml of the stock until completely smooth.
Add the blended beans, remaining stock, lentils, passata, tomato purée, sugar and Worcestershire to the pan.
Simmer for 25 minutes, stirring often, until the lentils have broken down and the stew is thick.
Serve over mash, topped with the grated cheddar.
tip: Blending the butter beans removes their skins from the equation while keeping the creaminess and protein. Look for smoked paprika labelled 'sweet' or 'dulce'.
swaps: Use blended cannellini beans instead of butter beans
Serve with soft polenta instead of mash

storage.text: Perfect for batch cooking. Keeps for 3 days in the fridge or freeze in portions for 3 months. Defrost in the fridge and reheat until piping hot, adding a splash of water.

title: Slow-cooker squash & chickpea tagine
summary: A warmly spiced Moroccan-style stew of soft squash and carrot, thickened with blended chickpeas and served with buttery couscous (slow-cooks for 6 hours).
ingredients: 500g butternut squash, peeled and cut into 2cm chunks
steps: Soften the onion in the oil in a frying pan for 8–10 minutes, adding the garlic for the last minute.
Blend the chickpeas with 200ml of the stock until completely smooth.
Put the softened onion and garlic, squash, carrots, blended chickpeas, remaining stock, lentils, passata, cumin, cinnamon, ginger, paprika and honey into the slow cooker and stir.
Cover and cook on low for 6 hours until the vegetables are very soft. Stir in the lemon juice and season with salt.
Just before serving, put the couscous in a bowl with the butter, pour over the hot stock, cover and leave for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Serve the tagine over the couscous, lightly mashing the squash if you like it softer.
tip: Long, slow cooking makes the squash and carrot meltingly soft, and blending the chickpeas means no skins. Fluff the couscous with extra butter or stock for a softer texture.
swaps: Use peeled sweet potato instead of squash
Serve with soft mash instead of couscous

storage.text: Great for batch cooking. Keep the tagine in the fridge for 3 days or freeze in portions for 3 months; defrost in the fridge and reheat until piping hot. Make the couscous fresh.

title: Paneer tikka traybake
summary: A Friday-night fakeaway of mildly spiced yoghurt-marinated paneer roasted with soft potatoes and peeled sweet peppers.
ingredients: 600g potatoes, peeled and cut into 2cm chunks
steps: Mix the yoghurt, curry powder, garam masala, paprika, garlic, ginger and lemon juice. Stir in the paneer and leave to marinate while the veg cooks.
Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Put the whole peppers and the potatoes on a large tray, toss the potatoes in the oil and a pinch of salt and roast for 30 minutes.
Move the peppers to a bowl, cover with a plate for 10 minutes, then peel off the skins, discard the seeds and slice the flesh.
Add the paneer to the tray with the potatoes and roast for 15 minutes until hot and golden at the edges.
Toss in the peeled peppers and serve with warm naan.
tip: Roasting the peppers whole makes their skins slip off easily, leaving just the soft, sweet flesh. The spice blend is fragrant rather than hot.
swaps: Use halloumi or firm tofu instead of paneer
Swap the peppers for peeled courgette chunks, roasted with the potatoes

storage.text: Best eaten fresh. Keep leftovers in the fridge for up to 2 days and reheat in a hot oven until piping hot. Not suitable for freezing.

title: Gentle sweet & sour tofu
summary: Golden tofu and soft peeled peppers in a glossy, tangy-sweet takeaway-style sauce.
ingredients: 400g firm tofu, pressed and cut into 2cm cubes
3 tbsp cornflour, plus 1 tsp for the sauce
1 red pepper, peeled with a speed peeler, deseeded and sliced
1 yellow pepper, peeled with a speed peeler, deseeded and sliced
steps: Toss the tofu in 3 tbsp cornflour. Fry in 2 tbsp of the oil in a large non-stick frying pan for 8–10 minutes, turning, until golden. Set aside.
Add the remaining oil, the peppers, carrot and onion with a splash of water. Cover and cook for 8–10 minutes, stirring, until very soft.
Whisk the orange juice, ketchup, vinegar, sugar, soy and 1 tsp cornflour, pour into the pan and bubble for 2 minutes until glossy.
Return the tofu, toss to coat and serve with rice.
tip: Peeling the peppers with a speed peeler and covering them as they cook makes them soft and skin-free. Pick a ketchup with a short ingredient list.
swaps: Use cubes of halloumi instead of tofu
Serve with soft egg noodles instead of rice

storage.text: Keep the tofu and sauce in the fridge for up to 2 days and reheat until piping hot. Cool leftover rice within 1 hour, keep in the fridge, eat within 1 day and reheat only once. Don't freeze.

title: Quick yoghurt-dough margherita pizza
summary: No-yeast, two-ingredient pizza bases topped with a simple garlicky tomato sauce and melting mozzarella.
ingredients: 250g self-raising flour, plus extra for dusting
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) and put two baking trays in to heat.
Mix the flour, yoghurt and salt into a soft dough. Knead briefly on a floured surface, halve and roll each into a thin 25cm round.
Stir together the passata, garlic, oregano and olive oil.
Carefully place the bases on the hot trays, spread with the sauce and top with the mozzarella and cheddar.
Bake for 12–15 minutes until the base is golden and the cheese is bubbling.
tip: A takeaway-style pizza with a plain white base and no spicy toppings. Add soft, peeled and pre-cooked courgette slices if you want some veg.
swaps: Top with thin slices of peeled, roasted courgette before baking
Use ricotta dotted over instead of cheddar

storage.text: Keep leftover slices in the fridge for 2 days and reheat in a hot oven until piping hot. Baked, cooled pizzas can be wrapped and frozen for 1 month; reheat from frozen in a hot oven.

title: Mild satay noodles with tofu
summary: Egg noodles, soft peeled veg and tofu tossed in a creamy, smooth peanut and lime sauce.
ingredients: 1 carrot, peeled and cut into ribbons with a peeler
1 courgette, peeled and cut into ribbons with a peeler
steps: Toss the tofu in the cornflour and fry in 1 tbsp of the oil for 8 minutes until golden. Set aside.
Add the remaining oil, carrot and courgette ribbons with a splash of water. Cover and cook for 6–8 minutes until very soft, then stir in the spinach to wilt.
Meanwhile, cook the noodles according to the packet and drain.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy, honey, lime juice, ginger and hot water until smooth.
Toss the noodles, veg, tofu and sauce together in the pan over a low heat until coated and hot.
tip: Smooth peanut butter gives all the satay flavour without any nut pieces. Choose one that's just peanuts and a little salt.
swaps: Use smooth cashew butter instead of peanut butter
Swap the tofu for sliced omelette

storage.text: Keep leftovers in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat with a splash of water until piping hot, or eat cold. Not suitable for freezing.

title: Leek & cheddar crustless quiche
summary: A soft, set savoury custard with melting leeks and cheddar, no pastry needed.
ingredients: 2 leeks (white and pale green parts only), halved lengthways and very finely sliced
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and grease a 23cm ovenproof dish.
Melt the butter in a pan and cook the leeks gently, covered, for 12–15 minutes until very soft. Spread over the base of the dish.
Whisk the flour with a little of the milk until smooth, then whisk in the remaining milk, the eggs, most of the cheese and the nutmeg. Season with salt and pepper.
Pour over the leeks, scatter with the rest of the cheese and bake for 30–35 minutes until just set with a slight wobble.
Leave to settle for 5 minutes before slicing.
tip: No pastry keeps it lighter, and the leeks are cooked slowly until silky. Slice them very finely so there are no stringy pieces.
swaps: Use peeled, grated courgette (squeezed dry) instead of leeks
Swap the cheddar for crumbled feta

storage.text: Cool quickly, cover and keep in the fridge for up to 2 days. Eat cold or reheat until piping hot. Don't freeze — the egg custard turns watery.

title: Lentil-stuffed courgette boats
summary: Peeled courgette halves baked until tender and filled with a herby tomato and lentil sauce under bubbling mozzarella.
ingredients: 4 medium courgettes, peeled and halved lengthways
20g vegetarian Italian-style hard cheese, finely grated
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Scoop out the soft centres of the courgettes with a teaspoon and finely chop the scooped flesh.
Lay the courgette halves cut-side up in a baking dish, cover with foil and bake for 15 minutes to soften.
Meanwhile, soften the onion in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the garlic, chopped courgette flesh, lentils, passata, stock and oregano and simmer for 20 minutes until thick. Season with salt and pepper.
Spoon the lentil sauce into the courgettes, top with the mozzarella and hard cheese and bake uncovered for 20 minutes until golden and the courgettes are very soft.
tip: Peeling the courgettes before baking means the whole boat is soft enough to cut with a spoon. Spoon any extra filling around the courgettes in the dish.
swaps: Use peeled marrow, cut into thick rings, instead of courgettes
Top with crumbled feta instead of mozzarella

storage.text: Keep leftovers in the fridge for up to 2 days and reheat until piping hot. Don't freeze — the baked courgettes go watery.

title: Red lentil & ricotta balls in tomato sauce
summary: Tender baked lentil and cheese 'meatballs' simmered in a rich tomato sauce, served over spaghetti.
ingredients: 30g vegetarian Italian-style hard cheese, finely grated
steps: Simmer the lentils in the water for 15 minutes, stirring often, until soft and all the water is absorbed. Spread on a plate to cool for 10 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Mix the lentils with the ricotta, breadcrumbs, hard cheese, egg, half the garlic and 1 tsp of the oregano. Season and roll into 16 balls.
Place on a lined tray, brush with 1 tbsp of the oil and bake for 20 minutes until firm and golden.
Meanwhile, warm the remaining oil and cook the rest of the garlic for 1 minute. Add the passata, sugar and remaining oregano and simmer for 15 minutes.
Cook the spaghetti according to the packet. Add the baked balls to the sauce, simmer gently for 5 minutes and serve over the spaghetti.
tip: The lentils break down completely, so the balls are soft enough to cut with a fork. If the mixture feels too wet to roll, add a few more breadcrumbs.
swaps: Use 50g grated cheddar instead of ricotta
Serve over soft polenta or mash instead of spaghetti

storage.text: Freeze the balls in their sauce for up to 3 months; defrost in the fridge and reheat until piping hot. Keeps for 3 days in the fridge. Cook the pasta fresh.

title: Lentil casserole with cheesy dumplings
summary: A hearty, thick red lentil, carrot and potato casserole topped with fluffy cheddar and thyme dumplings.
ingredients: 3 carrots, peeled and cut into chunks
400g potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
steps: Soften the onion in the oil in a large casserole pan for 10 minutes.

Add the carrots, potatoes, lentils, stock, tomato purée, Worcestershire, 1 tsp of the thyme and the bay leaf. Season and simmer, covered, for 25 minutes until the vegetables are tender and the lentils have thickened the gravy.
Meanwhile, mix the flour, butter, cheese and remaining thyme with a pinch of salt. Stir in enough milk to make a soft, sticky dough and shape into 8 balls.
Remove the bay leaf. Sit the dumplings on top of the casserole, cover with a lid and simmer gently for 20 minutes until they are risen and fluffy.
Serve in bowls.
tip: Cook the vegetables until they mash easily with a fork. Steaming the dumplings under the lid keeps them soft rather than crusty.
swaps: Use peeled butternut squash instead of potatoes
Leave the cheese out of the dumplings and stir it into the casserole instead

storage.text: Freeze the casserole without the dumplings in portions for up to 3 months; defrost in the fridge, reheat until piping hot and add freshly made dumplings. Leftovers with dumplings keep for 3 days in the fridge.

title: Banana semolina breakfast bowl
summary: Warm, silky semolina cooked in milk with mashed ripe banana and a pinch of cinnamon.
steps: Warm the milk in a small pan until steaming.
Sprinkle in the semolina, whisking all the time, then simmer gently for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until thick and smooth.
Mash the banana very smoothly with a fork and stir it into the semolina with the cinnamon.
Spoon into a bowl and drizzle with honey or maple syrup, if using.
tip: Semolina is a refined, low-fibre grain that cooks to a completely smooth texture. A really ripe, spotty banana mashes most smoothly and adds sweetness without much extra sugar.
swaps: Swap the banana for 3 tbsp smooth stewed pear or apple purée
Use oat or soya milk with added calcium instead of dairy milk

storage.text: Best eaten fresh, as it thickens as it stands. Fridge for up to 1 day and reheat with a splash of milk until piping hot.

title: Buttery coddled eggs with soft toast
summary: Eggs gently cooked in a buttered cup until just set, with fingers of lightly toasted white bread.
steps: Rub the butter around the inside of a ramekin or small heatproof cup.
Crack in the eggs and add the milk and salt.
Stand the ramekin in a small pan with hot water halfway up the sides, cover and simmer gently for 8–10 minutes until the whites are set.
Meanwhile, lightly toast the bread and cut it into fingers.
Stir the eggs gently with a teaspoon and eat with the soft toast.
tip: Gentle water-bath cooking keeps the eggs tender without frying. Toast the bread only lightly and remove the crusts so it stays soft.
swaps: Stir 1 tbsp grated mild cheddar into the eggs before cooking
Serve with a spoonful of smooth mashed potato instead of toast

storage.text: Eat straight away; don't keep or freeze.

title: Pastina in cheesy broth
summary: Tiny pasta stars cooked very soft in broth and made creamy with egg and grated cheese.
ingredients: 80g pastina or other tiny soup pasta, such as stelline
25g vegetarian Italian-style hard cheese, finely grated
steps: Bring the stock to the boil, add the pasta and simmer for 7–9 minutes, a minute or two past the packet time, until very soft.
Beat the egg with the cheese in a jug.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the butter, then slowly pour in the egg mixture, stirring all the time.
Return to a very low heat for 1–2 minutes, stirring, until the egg is cooked and the broth is creamy. Season with pepper, if using.
tip: Cooking the pasta a little past the packet time makes it extra soft. The egg adds protein to a small, easy bowl.
swaps: Use broken-up vermicelli instead of pastina
Leave out the egg and stir in 1 tbsp cream cheese instead

storage.text: Best fresh, as the pasta keeps soaking up the broth. Fridge for up to 1 day and reheat gently with a splash of water until piping hot.

title: Silky sweet potato & ginger soup
summary: Naturally sweet, golden soup with a gentle warmth from fresh ginger.
ingredients: 2cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and grated
steps: Soften the onion in the oil over a low heat for 8 minutes, then add the ginger for 1 minute.
Add the sweet potatoes and stock and simmer for 20 minutes until very soft.
Add the milk and blend until completely smooth. Season with salt and reheat gently.
tip: Peeled sweet potato blends to a silky texture with no fibrous bits. Keep the ginger to a small piece for warmth without heat.
swaps: Use peeled butternut squash instead of sweet potato
Swap the milk for 100ml light coconut milk

storage.text: Fridge for 3 days or freeze in portions for 3 months. Defrost in the fridge and reheat until piping hot.

title: Gnocchi in silky carrot sauce
summary: Pillowy potato gnocchi tossed in a sweet, smooth carrot and ricotta sauce.
ingredients: 15g vegetarian Italian-style hard cheese, finely grated
steps: Simmer the carrots in the stock for 15–18 minutes until very soft.
Blend the carrots and stock with the butter and ricotta to a silky sauce. Season and keep warm.
Cook the gnocchi in boiling salted water until they float, then 1 minute more, and drain.
Toss the gnocchi in the sauce and top with the grated cheese.
tip: Gnocchi are soft and easy to eat; pick a pack with a short ingredient list (mostly potato and flour). The sauce is light on fat but still creamy.
swaps: Use peeled butternut squash instead of carrots
Serve the sauce with soft-cooked small pasta shapes instead of gnocchi

storage.text: Fridge leftovers for up to 2 days and reheat until piping hot. The carrot sauce on its own freezes for 3 months; cook the gnocchi fresh.

title: Soft rice noodles in ginger broth with egg
summary: Fine rice noodles and very soft carrot in a light ginger-soy broth with silky egg ribbons.
ingredients: 1 carrot, peeled and cut into thin matchsticks
steps: Simmer the stock with the ginger and soy sauce for 5 minutes.
Add the carrot and simmer for 8 minutes until very soft.
Meanwhile, soak the noodles as the packet says, drain, then add to the broth for 1–2 minutes until very soft. Remove the ginger slices.
Beat the eggs and drizzle into the simmering broth, stirring gently, and cook for 1 minute until set.
Snip the noodles into short lengths with clean scissors and serve with a few drops of sesame oil, if using.
tip: Snipping the noodles short makes them easier to eat slowly and chew well. Sesame oil is fine — it's the whole seeds to leave out.
swaps: Use 150g cubed silken tofu instead of egg
Swap the carrot for a peeled, finely sliced courgette

storage.text: Best eaten fresh as the noodles soften further. Fridge for up to 1 day and reheat until piping hot. Don't freeze.

title: Smooth yellow moong dal
summary: Split yellow lentils simmered until they collapse into a mild, buttery, soup-like dal.
ingredients: 200g split yellow moong dal, rinsed well
White rice or soft white chapati, to serve
steps: Put the dal, water and turmeric in a pan. Bring to the boil, skim off any foam, then simmer for 25–30 minutes, stirring now and then, until completely broken down.
Whisk hard or blend until smooth, adding a splash of water if it's too thick.
Melt the butter in a small pan and cook the cumin and ginger gently for 1 minute without browning.
Stir the spiced butter into the dal with the salt and lemon juice. Serve with rice or soft chapati.
tip: Split moong dal has no skins and breaks down into a smooth purée. Keep it loose and soupy on a sore day.
swaps: Use red lentils instead of moong dal
Swap the cumin for 1/2 tsp mild curry powder

storage.text: The dal keeps 3 days in the fridge or freezes for 3 months; reheat until piping hot. If serving with rice, cool leftover rice within 1 hour, fridge and eat within 1 day, reheat only once and don't freeze it.

title: Warm honey & cinnamon milk
summary: A comforting mug of warm milk with honey and cinnamon, boosted with a little milk powder.
ingredients: 1 tbsp skimmed milk powder (optional, for extra protein)
steps: Whisk the milk powder and cinnamon into the cold milk in a small pan.
Heat gently until steaming but not boiling.
Take off the heat, stir in the honey and vanilla and pour into a mug.
tip: Milk powder adds protein without adding volume. Sip slowly and keep the cinnamon to a pinch.
swaps: Use soya milk with added calcium
Stir in 1 tsp smooth peanut butter for extra energy

storage.text: Make fresh each time.

title: Silky apple & pear purée
summary: Peeled apples and pears stewed and blended into a smooth, naturally sweet purée.
ingredients: 2 eating apples, peeled, cored and chopped
2 ripe pears, peeled, cored and chopped
steps: Put the fruit, water and cinnamon in a pan, cover and simmer gently for 12–15 minutes until very soft.
Blend or mash until completely smooth.
Serve warm or cool, on its own or stirred through porridge.
tip: Peeling and stewing the fruit makes it soft and smooth; sweet eating apples mean no added sugar is needed.
swaps: Use tinned peaches in juice instead of pears (no cooking needed)
Add a few drops of vanilla extract instead of cinnamon

storage.text: Fridge in a covered pot for 3 days, or freeze in ice-cube trays or small pots for 3 months.

title: Pear & ginger crumble
summary: Soft stewed pears with warm ginger under a buttery, fine crumble.
ingredients: 6 ripe pears (about 1kg), peeled, cored and chopped
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan).
Simmer the pears, caster sugar, ginger and water in a covered pan for 8–10 minutes until soft. Tip into an ovenproof dish.
Rub the butter into the flour until it looks like fine breadcrumbs, then stir in the brown sugar.
Scatter the crumble over the fruit and bake for 25–30 minutes until golden and bubbling.
tip: The topping is made without oats so it stays fine and sandy rather than chewy. Serving with custard softens it further.
swaps: Use peeled eating apples instead of pears
Use cinnamon instead of ginger

storage.text: Fridge for 3 days or freeze (cooked or uncooked) for 3 months. Reheat until piping hot.

title: Victoria sponge with seedless jam
summary: A classic light sponge sandwiched with smooth jam and vanilla buttercream.
ingredients: 200g butter, softened, plus extra for greasing
200g icing sugar, plus extra for dusting
5 tbsp smooth apricot jam or other seedless jam
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Grease and line two 20cm sandwich tins.
Beat the 200g butter, caster sugar, eggs, flour, baking powder and milk together until smooth.
Divide between the tins and bake for 20–22 minutes until golden and springy. Cool for 10 minutes in the tins, then on a rack.
Beat the 100g butter with the icing sugar and vanilla until pale and fluffy.
Spread the jam over one sponge and the buttercream over the other, sandwich together and dust with icing sugar.
tip: Check the jam label says seedless or smooth — apricot and blackcurrant jelly are easy to find without seeds.
swaps: Fill with whipped cream instead of buttercream (then keep it in the fridge)
Use lemon curd instead of jam

storage.text: Keep in an airtight tin in a cool place for 2 days. Unfilled sponges freeze, well wrapped, for 2 months; defrost and fill on the day.

title: Golden syrup sponge pudding
summary: A light, steamy sponge with a sticky golden syrup top, made quickly in the microwave.
ingredients: 100g butter, softened, plus extra for greasing
steps: Grease a 1.2 litre microwave-safe pudding basin and spoon the syrup into the bottom.
Beat the butter, sugar, eggs, flour, milk and vanilla together until smooth, then spoon over the syrup and level the top.
Cover loosely with a microwave-safe plate and cook on high (800W) for 5–6 minutes until risen and just set in the middle.
Leave to stand for 5 minutes, then turn out onto a plate.
tip: Serve with warm custard for a soft, comforting pudding. Microwave power varies, so check after 5 minutes.
swaps: Use 3 tbsp seedless jam instead of syrup
Steam on the hob for 1 1/2 hours, covered with pleated foil, instead of microwaving

storage.text: Fridge for 2 days, or freeze portions for 2 months. Reheat in the microwave in short bursts until piping hot.

title: Vanilla blancmange
summary: An old-fashioned set milk pudding thickened with cornflour (allow 3 hours to set).
steps: Mix the cornflour and sugar with 4 tbsp of the milk to a smooth paste.
Heat the rest of the milk until steaming, then pour it onto the paste, whisking.
Return to the pan and simmer, stirring constantly, for 2–3 minutes until thick.
Take off the heat, stir in the vanilla and pour into a rinsed mould or 4 small glasses.
Cool, cover and set in the fridge for 3 hours.
tip: Made with semi-skimmed milk it's low in fat but still silky, and sets without gelatine.
swaps: Add 1 tbsp cocoa powder with the cornflour for a chocolate version
Use soya milk with added calcium

storage.text: Keep covered in the fridge for 2 days. Don't freeze.

title: Vanilla tapioca pudding
summary: Soft, glossy tapioca pearls cooked slowly in milk with vanilla and nutmeg.
steps: Rinse the tapioca, put it in a pan with the milk and leave to soak for 15 minutes.
Bring slowly to a simmer and cook gently for 20–25 minutes, stirring often, until the pearls are clear and very soft.
Stir in the sugar and vanilla and cook for 2 minutes more.
Dust with nutmeg and serve warm or cold.
tip: Cook until every pearl is see-through and completely soft — there should be no firm centres.
swaps: Swirl in 2 tbsp smooth mango or peach purée
Use semolina instead of tapioca, cooking for 5 minutes

storage.text: Fridge covered for 2 days; it thickens when cold, so loosen with a splash of milk. Don't freeze.

title: Mango & yoghurt fool
summary: Silky mango purée rippled through whipped cream and Greek-style yoghurt.
ingredients: 425g tin mango slices in juice, drained
steps: Blend the mango with the lime juice until completely smooth.
Whip the cream with the icing sugar to soft peaks, then fold in the yoghurt.
Ripple most of the mango purée through the cream mixture.
Spoon into glasses and top with the remaining purée. Serve straight away or chill until needed.
tip: Mango has no seeds and blends perfectly smooth. Using half yoghurt keeps it lighter than an all-cream fool.
swaps: Use 1 large ripe fresh mango, peeled
Use smooth stewed apple purée instead of mango

storage.text: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 2 days. Don't freeze.

title: Lemon drizzle loaf
summary: A tender lemon loaf soaked with a sharp, sweet lemon drizzle.
ingredients: 175g butter, softened, plus extra for greasing
1 unwaxed lemon, finely zested and juiced
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Grease and line a 900g loaf tin.
Beat the butter, caster sugar, eggs, flour, milk and lemon zest together until pale and smooth.
Spoon into the tin and bake for 45–50 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Mix the lemon juice with the icing sugar.
Prick the warm cake all over with a skewer, spoon over the drizzle and leave to cool in the tin.
tip: Use a fine grater for the zest so there are no chewy strands, and icing sugar for a soft drizzle rather than a crunchy crust.
swaps: Use orange instead of lemon
Swap 2 tbsp of the milk for natural yoghurt for an even softer crumb

storage.text: Keep in an airtight tin for 3 days, or freeze slices, wrapped, for 2 months.

title: Soft spiced carrot cake
summary: A moist, gently spiced carrot cake with no nuts or dried fruit, topped with cream cheese frosting.
ingredients: 150ml sunflower oil, plus extra for greasing
200g carrots, peeled and very finely grated
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Grease and line a 20cm square tin.
Whisk the oil, brown sugar and eggs together, then stir in the carrot.
Fold in the flour, bicarbonate of soda, cinnamon and ginger until just combined.
Pour into the tin and bake for 35–40 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool completely.
Beat the butter and icing sugar together, then briefly beat in the cream cheese and vanilla. Spread over the cake.
tip: Grate the carrot on the finest side of the grater so it melts into the sponge as it bakes. No walnuts or raisins here.
swaps: Use peeled, finely grated courgette in place of half the carrot
Dust with icing sugar instead of frosting, then keep it in a tin

storage.text: With the frosting, keep covered in the fridge for 3 days. The un-iced cake freezes, wrapped, for 2 months.

title: Soft peanut butter cookies
summary: Chewy, soft-baked cookies made with smooth peanut butter (makes 16).
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and line two baking trays.
Beat the peanut butter, butter and sugar until creamy, then beat in the egg and vanilla.
Stir in the flour, bicarbonate of soda and salt to make a soft dough.
Roll into 16 balls, space well apart on the trays and flatten slightly.
Bake for 9–10 minutes until just set at the edges but still soft in the middle. Cool on the trays for 10 minutes, then on a rack.
tip: Always use smooth peanut butter, never crunchy. Taking them out while still soft keeps them tender rather than crisp.
swaps: Use smooth almond or cashew butter
Press a little seedless jam into each one before baking

storage.text: Keep in an airtight tin for 3 days. Freeze baked cookies, or balls of raw dough, for 3 months; bake dough from frozen for 1–2 minutes longer.

title: Peach frozen yoghurt
summary: A creamy, no-churn frozen yoghurt made by blending frozen tinned peaches with Greek yoghurt (allow 3 hours to freeze the fruit).
ingredients: 2 x 410g tins peach slices in juice, drained
steps: Spread the peaches on a lined tray and freeze for 3 hours until solid.
Blend the frozen peaches with the yoghurt, honey and lemon juice until smooth and thick, scraping down the sides as needed.
Eat straight away as soft-serve, or freeze in a lidded tub for 1 hour for firmer scoops.
tip: Peaches are peeled and seedless, so the result is completely smooth. Let it soften a little and eat slowly if very cold food bothers you.
swaps: Use tinned mango instead of peaches
Use maple syrup instead of honey

storage.text: Freeze in a lidded tub for up to 1 month; soften for 10–15 minutes before scooping. Don't refreeze once melted.

title: Honey & vanilla baked pears
summary: A lower-sugar pudding of peeled pears baked until meltingly tender in honeyed apple juice.
ingredients: 4 ripe pears, peeled, halved and cored
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan) and put the pears cut side up in an ovenproof dish.
Mix the honey, apple juice, vanilla and cinnamon and pour over the pears.
Cover with foil and bake for 25 minutes.
Uncover, spoon the juices over and bake for 10–15 minutes more until very tender. Serve warm with the juices.
tip: Peeled, baked pears are soft enough to cut with a spoon. Only 2 tbsp honey for four people keeps the added sugar low.
swaps: Use peeled, cored eating apples (bake 10 minutes longer)
Serve with a spoonful of natural yoghurt

storage.text: Fridge in their juices for 3 days; eat cold or reheat gently until hot. Not suited to freezing.

title: No-bake vanilla cheesecake pots
summary: Creamy vanilla cheesecake on a buttery shortbread base with a glossy apricot topping (allow 2 hours to firm up).
steps: Crush the shortbread to fine crumbs in a bag with a rolling pin, mix with the melted butter and press into the bottom of 4 small glasses.
Beat the cream cheese, yoghurt, icing sugar, vanilla and lemon juice together until smooth, then spoon over the bases.
Warm the jam with the water until runny and spoon over the top.
Cover and leave in the fridge for 2 hours to firm up.
tip: Shortbread crumbs soften under the creamy layer; avoid digestives, which are made with wholemeal flour. Pick a smooth, seedless jam.
swaps: Top with smooth mango purée instead of jam
Use rich tea biscuits instead of shortbread

storage.text: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 2 days. Don't freeze.

title: Apricot & white chocolate mousse
summary: A soft-set, creamy mousse of silken tofu, tinned apricots and a little white chocolate (allow 2 hours to set).
ingredients: 410g tin apricot halves in juice, drained
steps: Melt the chocolate in a bowl over a pan of barely simmering water, or in the microwave in short bursts.
Blend the tofu, apricots, honey and vanilla until completely smooth.
Add the melted chocolate and blend again briefly.
Pour into 4 small glasses, cover and set in the fridge for 2 hours.
tip: Silken tofu gives a creamy set without gelatine or cream, so it's lighter than a classic mousse. Tinned apricots are soft and peeled — check they're not the dried kind.
swaps: Use tinned peaches instead of apricots
Use maple syrup instead of honey

storage.text: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 2 days. Don't freeze.

title: Eve's pudding with custard
summary: Soft cinnamon apples baked under a light sponge, served warm with homemade vanilla custard.
ingredients: 4 eating apples (about 600g), peeled, cored and thinly sliced
100g butter, softened, plus extra for greasing
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and grease a 1.5 litre ovenproof dish.
Simmer the apples, 2 tbsp sugar, cinnamon and water in a covered pan for 5–8 minutes until softening, then tip into the dish.
Beat the butter, 100g sugar, eggs, flour and 2 tbsp milk together until smooth and spread over the apples.
Bake for 35–40 minutes until golden and springy.
Meanwhile, for the custard, whisk the egg yolks, cornflour and 40g sugar in a bowl. Heat the 500ml milk until steaming and whisk it onto the yolks.
Return the custard to the pan and stir over a low heat until thick, then stir in the vanilla. Serve the pudding warm with the custard.
tip: Pre-cooking the peeled apples means they're meltingly soft under the sponge. Use the spare egg whites in an omelette.
swaps: Use peeled pears instead of apples
Use 500ml ready-made fresh custard with a short ingredient list

storage.text: Fridge the pudding and custard separately for up to 2 days; reheat until piping hot. The pudding (without custard) freezes for 2 months; don't freeze the custard.

title: Chocolate self-saucing pudding
summary: A soft chocolate sponge that bakes on top of its own rich, glossy chocolate sauce.
ingredients: 75g butter, melted, plus extra for greasing
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and grease a 1.5 litre ovenproof dish.
Mix the flour, caster sugar and 3 tbsp cocoa in a bowl.
Whisk the milk, melted butter, egg and vanilla together, stir into the dry ingredients until smooth and spread in the dish.
Mix the brown sugar and 2 tbsp cocoa and sprinkle evenly over the top.
Carefully pour the boiling water over the back of a spoon onto the pudding — don't stir.
Bake for 30–35 minutes until the sponge is set on top with sauce underneath. Stand for 5 minutes before serving.
tip: Cocoa powder gives deep chocolate flavour with less fat than lots of chocolate. Serve small portions — it's rich.
swaps: Add 1 tsp instant coffee to the boiling water for a mocha version (if coffee suits you)
Use soya milk instead of dairy milk

storage.text: Fridge for up to 2 days and reheat in the microwave until piping hot (the sauce soaks in, so it becomes more fudgy). Not suited to freezing.

title: Peach & custard Sunday trifle
summary: A celebration trifle of jam-spread sponge, soft peaches, homemade custard and whipped cream (allow 3 hours for cooling and setting).
ingredients: 8 trifle sponges, or a 20cm plain sponge
150g smooth apricot jam or other seedless jam
2 x 410g tins peach slices in juice
steps: For the custard, whisk the egg yolks, cornflour and caster sugar in a bowl. Heat the milk until steaming and whisk it onto the yolks.
Return to the pan and stir over a low heat until thick. Stir in 1 tsp vanilla, cover the surface with baking paper to stop a skin forming and cool completely.
Split the sponges, spread with jam and arrange in the base of a 2 litre glass bowl.
Drain the peaches, keeping 6 tbsp of the juice. Spoon the juice over the sponge, then chop the peaches small and scatter over.
Pour the cooled custard over the fruit and leave in the fridge for 2 hours to set.
Whip the cream with the icing sugar and remaining 1 tsp vanilla to soft peaks, spread over the custard and finish with grated chocolate, if using.
tip: Everything here is soft and seedless, so it's a celebration pudding that suits the whole table. Pick trifle sponges with a short ingredient list, or bake your own.
swaps: Use sliced Victoria sponge with seedless jam instead of trifle sponges
Use tinned mango or pears instead of peaches

storage.text: Keep covered in the fridge and eat within 2 days. Don't freeze.

title: Mild Persian-style aubergine stew
summary: A gently spiced khoresh-style stew of melting peeled aubergine and yellow split peas in a lemony tomato sauce, served with basmati rice and yoghurt.
ingredients: 2 aubergines, peeled and cut into 2cm cubes
Pinch of saffron, soaked in 2 tbsp hot water (optional)
steps: Soften the onion in 1 tbsp of the oil in a large pan for 10 minutes. Add the garlic, turmeric, cinnamon and cumin and stir for 1 minute.
Add the split peas, tomato purée, passata and stock. Bring to the boil, then cover and simmer gently for 40 minutes, stirring now and then.
Meanwhile, cook the aubergine in the remaining oil in a frying pan with a splash of water, covered, for 10 minutes, stirring, until soft and lightly golden.
Add the aubergine to the stew and simmer, uncovered, for 20–25 minutes more until the split peas have collapsed and the aubergine is melting. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick.
Mash lightly with a potato masher, then stir in the lemon juice, sugar, saffron (if using) and salt to taste.
While the stew finishes, cook the rice according to the packet. Serve the stew over the rice with a spoonful of yoghurt.
tip: Traditionally this uses whole dried limes, which are hard to break down, so lemon juice gives the same sour note. Peeling the aubergine and cooking the split peas until they fall apart keeps it soft.
swaps: Use red lentils instead of split peas, simmering for 20 minutes before adding the aubergine
Use peeled courgette instead of aubergine

storage.text: The stew keeps for 3 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer; defrost in the fridge and reheat until piping hot. Cook rice fresh: if you keep leftover rice, cool it within 1 hour, eat within 1 day, reheat only once and don't freeze it.

title: Baked Glamorgan sausages
summary: Welsh cheese and leek 'sausages' bound with soft breadcrumbs and egg, baked rather than fried and easy to freeze in batches.
ingredients: 1 leek (white and pale green part only), halved lengthways and very finely sliced
150g Caerphilly or mild cheddar, finely grated
Buttery mash and gravy, to serve
steps: Melt the butter in a pan, add the leek, cover and cook gently for 12 minutes, stirring now and then, until completely soft. Leave to cool for 5 minutes.
Mix the breadcrumbs, cheese, thyme, mustard and cooked leek in a bowl and season with salt and pepper.
Stir in the eggs and milk to make a mixture that holds together when squeezed.
With damp hands, shape into 12 small sausages and roll each one lightly in the flour.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Put the sausages on a lined tray, brush with the oil and bake for 20–25 minutes, turning halfway, until golden.
Serve with buttery mash and gravy.
tip: Use plain white bread for the crumbs and cook the leek until silky so there are no stringy pieces. Baking gives a light golden outside without deep-frying.
swaps: Use crumbly Lancashire cheese instead of Caerphilly
Add 50g very finely chopped, well-wilted spinach (squeezed dry) to the mix

storage.text: Freeze uncooked sausages on a lined tray, then bag up and keep for 3 months; bake from frozen for 30–35 minutes until piping hot in the middle. Cooked sausages keep in the fridge for 2 days; reheat in the oven until piping hot.

title: Jam bread & butter pudding
summary: Buttered white bread layered with seedless jam and baked in a soft vanilla custard, with no raisins or peel.
ingredients: 30g butter, softened, plus extra for greasing
4 tbsp smooth apricot jam or other seedless jam
steps: Grease a 1.5 litre ovenproof dish. Butter the bread, spread with the jam and cut each slice into 4 triangles.
Arrange the triangles in the dish, overlapping, jam side up.
Whisk the eggs, milk, cream, sugar and vanilla, pour over the bread and press down gently. Leave to soak for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Dust the pudding with nutmeg and stand the dish in a roasting tin. Pour hot water from the kettle into the tin to come halfway up the dish.
Bake for 35–40 minutes until just set with a slight wobble. Leave to stand for 5 minutes before serving.
tip: Cutting off the crusts, soaking the bread well and baking in a water bath keeps the whole pudding soft, with no crisp edges. No dried fruit here — the jam adds the sweetness.
swaps: Use sliced brioche instead of white bread
Use lemon curd instead of jam

storage.text: Cool quickly, cover and keep in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat until piping hot. Don't freeze — the egg custard turns watery.
